budget.fits_note: simulation and control cells fit nothing (learned estimates are generated); the only fits are the matched fixture cell's 24 (eight estimators per representation plus the B = 1 identity control), development only; the production matrix plans 0 fits

replicates_declared.fixture: 3 MC replicates per cell at the fixture settings
replicates_declared.production_confirmation: 69 scenarios x 1000 MC replicates; per MC replicate at the archived setting: n_files x 2000 joint replicates, 4 x 10000 two-stage replicates, 4 x 28 x 400 block-curve replicates
replicates_declared.production_pilot: 8 scenarios x 2 settings x 200 MC replicates

budget.retry_policy: every attempt is charged at start; failed and interrupted attempts are never refunded; at most two retries per cell; simulation cells charge 0 fits so the cap constrains only the matched fixture cell (24 of 64)
budget.scale_formula: work_proxy_seconds(cell) = mc x [n_files x R_file x 180e-6 + 4 x R_hier x n_files x 2.3e-6 + n_dev x 28 x R_curve x 14e-6 + 0.001 (n_files + n_dev)] (constants measured in this container); scale = mean production work per cell / mean fixture work per cell; the confirmation scale divides production work at the archived setting by fixture work at the reduced setting (the setting a three-replicate fixture pilot freezes), so the confirmation estimate is an upper bound

calibration_tolerances.applies_to: coverage: the primary contrast raw-bin|empca on every confirmation scenario (pca|empca and zero|empca reported); type-I: every null claim on every null scenario and the any-null-claim rate
calibration_tolerances.evaluation: a scenario is within tolerance when its Wilson interval is not entirely outside the band; tolerances are fixed here, before the validation scenarios, and are copied unchanged into FROZEN_CALIBRATION.json

controls: simulator_estimand: with TRUE labels g rho the realised mean of each exact-mu contrast equals the declared mu within 4 Monte-Carlo standard errors
ar1_autocorrelation: the complex AR(1) generator has lag-one autocorrelation phi within 0.03 (phi = 0 and 0.6)
iid_bootstrap_se: at phi = 0 and block length 1 the joint bootstrap sd of a file mean equals the analytic sd/sqrt(n) within 25%

dependence_gate: with the dependence verdict forced to 'inconclusive' every claim is withheld; forced to 'stabilised' on the large effect at 4 files the denoising claim is supported (positive control)
holm_arithmetic: Holm step-down on a fixed p-set gives the known adjusted values

matched_fixture (development only): whole-window and band scoring share identical evaluation windows and labels, the six non-learned estimators are bit-identical across representations, and the B = 1 band identity control holds to 1e-12

estimands.bias: mean over replicates of (equal-file point estimate - mu) with its Monte-Carlo standard error and sign
estimands.coverage: P(ci95_lo <= mu <= ci95_hi) for the two-stage interval, unconditional and given not withheld; the same for the equal-file t-interval
estimands.length: mean interval length, two-stage versus t-interval
estimands.mu: equal-file mean of the per-file contrast E Delta_i over the file-sampling model lam_e,i = lam_e + tau b_i, N_i log-normal(mean 1): mu = lam_e * 4/w for raw-bin|empca, (lam_e - lam_p) * 4/w for pca|empca, lam_z * 4/w for zero|empca (physical-amplitude units; w = 1024 nominal)
estimands.power: P(claim verdict == 'supported') where the claim's contrasts have mu > 0, unconditional and given not withheld
estimands.type1: P(claim verdict == 'supported') on scenarios where every contrast of the claim has mu = 0; 'any' = P(at least one null claim supported)
estimands.withholding: P(aggregate dependence verdict == 'inconclusive'), reported separately from type-I error and power

explicitly_not_claimed: any change to the archived T22 verdicts (all withheld), intervals or p-values
adequacy of the archived inference on unexamined instrument data
that the synthetic dependence model (AR(1) plus optional random-walk drift) is the instrument's dependence structure
any instrument result from part B: the matched interface is exercised on synthetic HDF5 fixtures only, no hold-out exists in this container, and the release file list is an unresolved input
that a matched rerun on already exposed data would be independent evidence

failure_interpretation.adequacy_on_instrument_data: NOT established by any outcome here: the dependence structure of unexamined instrument data is unknown
failure_interpretation.control_failure: the run is not reducible (exit 4); the simulator or the wrapper is wrong, not the archived pipeline
failure_interpretation.coverage_outside_tolerance: the archived interval is not calibrated for that dependence/heterogeneity/file-count regime; reported as such, with the t-interval beside it; no re-tuning on confirmation seeds
failure_interpretation.feasibility_failure: the correct output of part B; it is reported as such
failure_interpretation.high_withholding: the procedure has no demonstrated useful power in that regime even if type-I is controlled; counted separately and fed into the feasibility rule
failure_interpretation.type1_above_tolerance: the declared decision rule over-claims in that regime; the archived verdicts (already withheld) are unaffected, and any future instrument run at that regime is infeasible

hypotheses: H1 (coverage): the two-stage 95% interval for the equal-file mean covers the declared estimand at a rate inside the tolerance band on every validation scenario without drift.
H2 (type-I): P(any null claim 'supported') is at or below 0.07 on every null scenario, and per null claim.

H3 (withholding): the withholding rate P(dependence inconclusive) is reported on every scenario; it is expected to rise with phi and to approach one under drift.  H3 is descriptive: no tolerance is set on it, but feasibility (below) uses it.

H4 (power): P('supported' | alternative) is reported for the small, medium and large effects at 4, 8 and 16 files, unconditionally and given not withheld.  No minimum is hypothesised; the feasibility rule uses the medium effect.
H5 (secondary): the equal-file Student-t interval and the random-effects interval are reported beside the primary for comparison of coverage and length.
H6 (bias): the sign of the bias of the equal-file point estimate is reported with its Monte-Carlo standard error.
independent_unit: Part A: one Monte-Carlo replicate (a fresh set of n_dev_files development files and n_files evaluation files); files within a replicate are independent draws of the declared file-sampling model and windows within a file are dependent by design.  Part B: one instrument file never opened by any archived stage; the exposure inventory shows which regions are already exposed, and a region of an already examined file is not an independent unit.

feasibility.rule: a matched instrument comparison is feasible at n available independent files only if n >= min_independent_files, the confirmation calibration is complete and within tolerance (type-I and primary coverage) at the largest calibrated n_files <= n, the maximum withholding rate over the non-drift scenarios at that n_files is <= max_withholding_rate, the power at the medium effect is >= min_power_medium_effect, and the development-data dependence verdict is not inconclusive; otherwise the output is a feasibility failure with its reasons, never an artificial four-file significance claim

inference.monte_carlo_uncertainty: Wilson score interval (z = 1.96) on every rate; the declared mc_replicates_per_scenario = 1000 gives half-width 0.0136 at a 5% rate (the smallest n with half-width <= 0.015 is 822)
inference.multiplicity: Holm-Bonferroni step-down at familywise 0.05 over the three claims (archived rule); a claim is 'supported' only if its point estimate favours EMPCA, its two-stage interval excludes zero and the Holm-adjusted p < 0.05, and the dependence verdict is not inconclusive

pilot_decision_rule.output: FROZEN_CALIBRATION.json in the run root, written by the pilot reducer only when every pilot cell is present; confirmation cells refuse to run without it and record its digest
pilot_decision_rule.purpose: choose the bootstrap replicate setting (per-file joint, two-stage file, block-curve replicates) before any confirmation cell is drawn; the block grids are the archived ones and are frozen unchanged
pilot_decision_rule.rule: freeze 'reduced' iff on EVERY pilot scenario the coverage of the primary contrast, the withholding rate and the any-supported rate differ between the two settings by at most the reference setting's Wilson half-width (paired seeds); otherwise freeze 'archived'

inference.pipeline: exactly the archived one, by import: te.fit_transfer -> te.squared_errors -> te.block_variance_curve on n_dev_files development files (4 contrasts each) and the calibration series -> te.aggregate_block_curves (maximum rule) -> te.select_block_length (frozen b_eval, b_cal, verdict) -> te.joint_bootstrap per evaluation file at the frozen block lengths -> te.percentile_interval -> t22.combine_stage (t22.hierarchical_file_bootstrap two-stage equal-file mean, t22.holm, verdict rules, t22.t_interval, t22.random_effects, te.combine_files)

scenario_model.heavy_tails_arm: t_3 innovations scaled to unit variance

archived_facts_unchanged: all three archived T22 verdicts are withheld (inconclusive) because the frozen dependence assessment did not stabilise (V(32)/V(16) = 1.745, curve still rising)
the archived intervals and p-values are conditional diagnostics, not claims
the archived whole-window versus narrowband comparison is unmatched (time region, file composition, evaluation length, selection and inference differ)
416 executions / 240 distinct fits against a cap of 250 are disclosed; nothing in this package re-executes any of them
T22 hold-out was a temporal hold-out on already examined files, not independent-file replication

provenance.no_prior_t22s_protocol: No T22-S protocol existed on 12 September 2026; the successor_20260912 round holds T19-S and T20-S protocols only.  This v2 file is the first T22-S protocol; the version label follows the round's naming convention, not a prior v1.

question: Does the archived T22 inference procedure (joint calibration/evaluation circular-block bootstrap per file, maximum-aggregated block-variance dependence gate, two-stage hierarchical file bootstrap of the equal-file mean, Holm across three claims) have nominal coverage, controlled type-I error and demonstrated useful power -- with its withholding rate counted separately -- on synthetic files with declared dependence, cross-unit heterogeneity and transfer-calibration uncertainty; and what does a matched real-data comparison need before it can be attempted?
seed_derivation: Monte-Carlo replicate j of a cell with seed s uses replicate seed s * 10000 + j (j < mc_replicates); the two pilot replicate settings of one chunk share s (paired comparison); confirmation chunks share their seeds across scenarios (common random numbers, declared).  Control cells are seedless and use the fixed internal stream 424242.
stopping_rule: fixed allocation: every pilot cell (8 scenarios x 2 settings x 200 Monte-Carlo replicates), then every confirmation cell (69 scenarios x 1000 Monte-Carlo replicates) and every control; no cell is added, dropped or repeated on the basis of an outcome; the only conditional step is the pre-declared replicate-setting freeze
title: T22-S (L4): synthetic calibration of the archived T22 inference pipeline and a matched whole-window/narrowband real-data interface
